arxiv-1509-04781.title: Dirichlet Fragmentation Processes: A Useful Variant of Fragmentation Processes for Modelling Hierarchical Data
arxiv-1509-04781.creator: Hong Ge, Yarin Gal, Zoubin Ghahramani
arxiv-1509-04781.description: Abstract Tree structures are ubiquitous in data across many domains, and many datasets are naturally modelled by unobserved tree structures. In this paper, first we review the theory of random fragmentation processes [ Bertoin 2006 ] , and a number of existing methods for modelling trees, including the popular nested Chinese restaurant process (nCRP).

arxiv-1607-06027.title: New Approach to Metal–Insulator Phase Transition Kinetics in Magnetic Field.
arxiv-1607-06027.creator: L.B. Dubovskii
arxiv-1607-06027.description: Abstract The metal–insulator phase transition is considered on the basis of Ginzburg-Landau type equations with two different order parameters. An inclusion of magnetic field in this picture is an important step for understanding of behavior of the metal–insulator phase transition kinetics.

arxiv-2007-02341.title: Large deviations of the ballistic Lévy walk model
arxiv-2007-02341.creator: Wanli Wang, Marc Höll, Eli Barkai
arxiv-2007-02341.description: Abstract We study the ballistic Lévy walk stemming from an infinite mean traveling time between collision events. Our study focuses on the density of spreading particles all starting from a common origin, which is limited by a ‘light’ cone − v 0 ​ t < x < v 0 ​ t -v_{0}t<x<v_{0}t .

arxiv-2011-14044.title: A Deductive Verification Framework For Higher Order Programs
arxiv-2011-14044.creator: Tiago Soares — 52965, Supervisors: Mário Pereira, António Ravara
arxiv-2011-14044.description: Abstract In this report, we present the preliminary work developed for our research project for the APDC ( Área Prática de Desenvolvimento Curricular ) course. The main goal of this project is to develop a framework, on top of the Why3 tool, for the verification of effectful higher-order programs.

arxiv-2012-01193.title: Black Loans Matter: Distributionally Robust Fairness for Fighting Subgroup Discrimination
arxiv-2012-01193.creator: Mark Weber, Mikhail Yurochkin, Sherif Botros, Vanio Markov
arxiv-2012-01193.description: Abstract Algorithmic fairness in lending today relies on group fairness metrics for monitoring statistical parity across protected groups. This approach is vulnerable to subgroup discrimination by proxy, carrying significant risks of legal and reputational damage for lenders and blatantly unfair outcomes for borrowers. Practical challenges arise from the many possible combinations and subsets of protected groups.

arxiv-2012-02505.title: Financial Document Causality Detection Shared Task (FinCausal 2020)
arxiv-2012-02505.creator: Dominique Mariko 1 Hanna Abi-Akl 1 Estelle Labidurie 1 Stéphane Durfort 1 Hugues de Mazancourt 1 Mahmoud El-Haj 2 1 YseopLab, FR, 2 Lancaster University, UK, 1 lab@yseop.com, 2 m.el-haj@lancaster.ac.uk
arxiv-2012-02505.description: Abstract We present the FinCausal 2020 Shared Task on Causality Detection in Financial Documents and the associated FinCausal dataset, and discuss the participating systems and results. Two sub-tasks are proposed: a binary classification task (Task 1) and a relation extraction task (Task 2).

arxiv-2102-07588.title: Jovian Auroral Radio Source Occultation Modelling and Application to the JUICE Science Mission Planning Journal: Planetary and Space Sciences
arxiv-2102-07588.creator: Baptiste Cecconi, Corentin K. Louis, Claudio Muñoz Crego, Claire Vallat
arxiv-2102-07588.description: Abstract Occultations of the Jovian low frequency radio emissions by the Galilean moons have been observed by the PWS instrument of the Galileo spacecraft. We show that the ExPRES (Exoplanetary and Planetary Radio Emission Simulator) code accurately models the temporal occurrence of the occultations in the whole spectral range observed by Galileo/PWS. This validates of the ExPRES code.

arxiv-2105-01750.title: Optimal Real-time Coordination of Distributed Energy Resources in Low-voltage Grids
arxiv-2105-01750.creator: Sen Zhan 1 , Johan Morren 1 2 , Wouter van den Akker 1 3 , Anne van der Molen 1 4 , and Han Slootweg 1 2
arxiv-2105-01750.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sen Zhan 1 , Johan Morren 1 2 , Wouter van den Akker 1 3 , Anne van der Molen 1 4 , and Han Slootweg 1 2. This study proposes a real-time distributed energy resource (DER) coordination model that can exploit flexibility from the DERs to solve voltage and overloading issues using both active and reactive power.

arxiv-2303-15452.title: The radiation environment over the African continent at aviation altitudes: First results of the RPiRENA-based dosimeter
arxiv-2303-15452.creator: M.G. Mosotho, R.D. Strauss, S. Böttcher, C. Diedericks
arxiv-2303-15452.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by M.G. Mosotho, R.D. Strauss, S. Böttcher, C. Diedericks. The radiation environment over the African continent, at aviation altitudes, remains mostly uncharacterized and unregulated. In this paper we present initial measurements made by a newly developed active dosimeter on-board long-haul flights between South Africa and Germany. Based on these initial tests, we believe that this low-cost and open-source dosimeter is suitable for continued operation over the Africa continent and can provide valuable long-term measurements to test dosimteric models and inform aviation policy.

arxiv-2410-01021.title: A Naturally-Colored Translation from LTL to Parity and COCOA Thanks: Supported by DFG through Grant No. 322591867 (GUISynth) and the BMWi through Grant No. 19A21026E (SafeWahr).
arxiv-2410-01021.creator: Rüdiger Ehlers, Ayrat Khalimov
arxiv-2410-01021.description: Abstract Chains of co-Büchi automata (COCOA) have recently been introduced as a new canonical representation of omega-regular languages. The co-Büchi automata in a chain assign to each omega-word its natural color, which depends only on the language itself and not on its automaton representation.

arxiv-2411-10956.title: IVE: Enhanced Probabilistic Forecasting of Intraday Volume Ratio with Transformers
arxiv-2411-10956.creator: Hanwool Lee, Heehwan Park
arxiv-2411-10956.description: Abstract This paper presents a new approach to volume ratio prediction in financial markets, specifically targeting the execution of Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) strategies. Recognizing the importance of accurate volume profile forecasting, our research leverages the Transformer architecture to predict intraday volume ratio at a one-minute scale.

arxiv-2507-08856.title: A self-contained proof of the Artin-Wedderburn theorem in the case of finite-dimensional Von Neumann algebras
arxiv-2507-08856.creator: Octave Mestoudjian, Pablo Arrighi
arxiv-2507-08856.description: Abstract We provide a self-contained proof of the Artin-Wedderburn theorem in the case of finite-dimensional Von Neumann algebras (or equivalently unital C* algebras) that is fully constructive and uses only basic notions of linear algebra. The Artin-Wedderburn theorem, originally stated in [ 1 ] and [ 6 ] , is a fundamental theorem on the strucutre of (semi-simple) rings.

arxiv-2510-21101.title: Tunable Asymmetric Delay Attack in Quantum Clock Synchronization
arxiv-2510-21101.creator: Hui Han, Haotian Teng, Hailong Xu, Jinquan Huang, Yuanmei Xie, Yichen Zhang, Bo Liu, Wanrong Yu, Baokang Zhao, Shuhui Chen
arxiv-2510-21101.description: Abstract Quantum clock synchronization underpins modern secure communications and critical infrastructure, yet its fundamental dependence on channel reciprocity introduces an exploitable vulnerability to asymmetric delay attacks. Current attack strategies rely on static delays, limiting their ability to target application-specific stability requirements. Here, we propose a tunable asymmetric delay attack (T-ADA) that dynamically controls delay parameters to induce manipulate synchronization accuracy.

arxiv-2601-03588.title: AR Object Layout Method Using Miniature Room Generated from Depth Data
arxiv-2601-03588.creator: K. Ihara 1 and I. Kawaguchi 1 1 University of Tsukuba, Japan
arxiv-2601-03588.description: Abstract In augmented reality (AR), users can place virtual objects anywhere in a real-world room, called AR layout. Although several object manipulation techniques have been proposed in AR, it is difficult to use them for AR layout owing to the difficulty in freely changing the position and size of virtual objects.

plos-pone-0360527.title: The association between prenatal maternal selenium concentration and mental health in early childhood, a mother-child cohort study
plos-pone-0360527.creator: Suman Ranjitkar, Ingrid Kvestad, Ram K Chandyo, Kjersti S Bakken, Manjeswori Ulak, Tor A Strand, Sandra Huber, Maria Averina
plos-pone-0360527.description: The association between prenatal maternal selenium concentration and mental health in early childhood, a mother-child cohort study

pmc-10607066.title: Synthesizing Human Activity for Data Generation
pmc-10607066.creator: Ana Romero, Pedro Carvalho, Luís Côrte-Real, Américo Pereira, Hojjat Salehinejad
pmc-10607066.description: The problem of gathering sufficiently representative data, such as those about human actions, shapes, and facial expressions, is costly and time-consuming and also requires training robust models. This has led to the creation of techniques such as transfer learning or data augmentation. However, these are often insufficient.

pmc-11476692.title: Comparison of the risk of noise-induced hearing loss between male police officers and male non-police officers: a nationwide cohort study using propensity score matching in South Korea
pmc-11476692.creator: Woo-Ri Lee, Kyu-Tae Han, Ki-Bong Yoo, Jin-Ha Yoon
pmc-11476692.description: BackgroundPolice officers are at a high risk of noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) owing to the nature of their work. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the risk of NIHL in police officers and controls.MethodsThis study used the National Health Insurance claims data of workers aged 25–65 years obtained from 2005 to 2015.

pmc-11606235.title: The relationship between dyadic coping and post-traumatic growth in breast cancer patients and spouses: based on potential profile analysis
pmc-11606235.creator: Yefan Zhang, Yuqi Gao, Ning Zhang, Kaiyan Xu, Shuo Zhao
pmc-11606235.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe disease impact of breast cancer is to view the couple as a whole, breast cancer is a disease shared by the couple. Cancer coping has evolved from an individual perspective to a dyadic coping perspective for couples.

pmc-11709628.title: The relationship between amyloid‐b and cognition in young‐onset Mild Cognitive Impairment: the influence of disease duration
pmc-11709628.creator: Chiara Carbone, Erica Balboni, Daniela Beltrami, Manuela Tondelli, Chiara Gallingani, Federico Gasparini, Davide Salvatori, Simone Salemme, Giulia Vinceti, Alessandro Fraternali, Alessandro Marti, Annalisa Chiari, Giovanna Zamboni
pmc-11709628.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe effect of amyloid‐b brain deposition on cognition is still debated, since it has been shown that its accumulation begins almost 15 years before cognitive symptoms' onset, then reaches a plateau while cognition continues to decline.

pmc-12495623.title: Tetrahydropalmatine has analgesic role in mouse model of bone cancer pain by inactivating the TNF-α/uPA/PAR2/TRPV1 pathway in dorsal root ganglia
pmc-12495623.creator: Guangda Zheng, Linghan Meng, Lu Shang, Juanxia Ren, Dongtao Li, Yanju Bao
pmc-12495623.description: BackgroundTreatment of bone cancer pain (BCP) remains a challenge. The current paper was to research the analgesic effect of Tetrahydropalmatine (THP) on BCP and the related mechanisms.MethodsMouse model of BCP was constructed by injecting E0771 breast cancer cells into the tibia. Behavioral test was performed to research the effect of THP on pain nociception of BCP mice.

pmc-12837036.title: Epigenetics of glaucoma in the trabecular meshwork
pmc-12837036.creator: Zhihao Liu, Yajuan Zheng, Jing Zhao
pmc-12837036.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Glaucoma represents a predominant cause of irreversible blindness globally, characterized by the association of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and retinal ganglion cell loss with dysfunction of the trabecular meshwork (TM), the principal tissue regulating conventional aqueous humor outflow. Emerging evidence suggests that this dysfunction is not exclusively driven by genetic variation or mechanical stress; rather, it is significantly influenced by epigenetic mechanisms that integrate factors such as aging, hypoxia/oxidative stress, glucocorticoid exposure, and other environmental challenges into enduring alterations in TM phenotype.

pmc-13230852.title: Contact-induced continuous electricity generation by ion-electron positive feedback coupled transport for self-powered ionic touch panel
pmc-13230852.creator: Kedong Shang, Jiahao Fang, Xiaobo Pu, Peng Wang, Yao Chen, Hai Liu, Ning Zhang, Junjie Hao, Yong Zhang, Bingjun Yu, Linmao Qian, Tingting Yang
pmc-13230852.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ionic touch panels are regarded as a key platform for future human-computer interaction and meta-universe due to their stretchable, transparent and skin-fitting properties. Inspired by the fact that human skin relies on ionic current to sense contact position information, we have investigated an ionogel based closed-loop electrical system that also converts contact into ionic current to form a self-powered single-layer ionic touch panel.

pmc-13273611.title: A Closed-Loop Audit of Electronic Discharge Summary Completeness and Safety Netting at Queen Alia Military Hospital in Jordan
pmc-13273611.creator: Murad M Hamiedah, Abdallah H Khamash, Ahmad Ibrahim Al-Arman, Omar J Haddad
pmc-13273611.description: BackgroundSafe discharge from the hospital is a critical component of patient safety and affects continuity of care. Following discharge, surgical patients remain at risk of developing some complications and may be uncertain about their expected recovery. Clear, structured discharge information will help them understand the post-discharge pathway, recognize warning symptoms, and seek timely medical review.
